title: keys / values / entries
description: Walk a plain object with Object.keys / values / entries, for…in, and destructuring inside loops.

notes: for…in walks the prototype chain — it can surface inherited keys. Object.keys does NOT.
Numeric-looking keys are iterated in ascending numeric order, then string keys in insertion order.
Entries pair beautifully with destructuring: for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(o)).

questions.q: Which iterator can pick up INHERITED keys?
questions.explain: for…in walks the prototype chain; the Object.* helpers stop at own keys.

questions.q: How do you rebuild an object from [["x",1],["y",2]]?
Inside `for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(o))`, what is `v`?

exercises.prompt: Sum all values of an object using Object.values.
Iterate object entries with destructuring — the load-bearing call is `Object.entries`.

L3.prompt: Write `invert(obj)` that swaps keys and values. Log `JSON.stringify(invert({ a: 1, b: 2, c: 3 }))`.
